clue.text: Put thousands of pounds on relative

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds, so several thousands are grands

explanation.surface: Someone bets a fortune on a family member, as if backing a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put ... on' reads like placing a bet, but 'Put' is only a link and 'on' supplies its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's son is a family member, so he is a relative.

clue.text: Criticises stage being rear ranged before time

indicators.note: placed before means this piece comes first in the answer
split as 'rear ranged' it hides the word rearranged, telling us to shuffle the letters of stage

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a theatre stage was set up back to front just before curtain-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rear ranged' is the word rearranged with a space slipped in, disguised as a description of a back-to-front stage; it makes GETSA.
explanation.definitionFit: To get at someone is an idiom for nagging or criticising them.

clue.text: Inclined to run after Asian

indicators.note: coming after means this piece follows the other in the answer

parts.note: AS is a standard abbreviation for Asian
to lope is to run with long easy strides

explanation.surface: Someone is tempted to chase after an Asian visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on a slant or slope is tilted, which is what inclined means here.

clue.text: Lump a toy with work

parts.note: a doll is a child's toy
OP, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A child's plaything is combined with a task.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollop is a shapeless blob or lump of something soft, such as food.

clue.text: Arouse hope anew for theatre

indicators.note: making something anew means making it over again in a fresh form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plea to make people excited and optimistic again about a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A building where operas are staged is a kind of theatre.

clue.text: Pull out the food's arrived

parts.note: grub is informal for food; the 's is read as is
up can mean having come or arrived, as in 'the sun is up'

explanation.surface: A dinner bell: the meal has turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull out' is the definition: to grub up is to dig a plant out by its roots.
explanation.definitionFit: To grub up a plant or stump is to dig it out of the ground by the roots.

clue.text: Glad deer live wild

indicators.note: wild suggests something out of control, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone is happy that the deer are living free in the wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling relief after worry is being glad that things turned out well.

clue.text: Behave in a more hysterical way and confuse utterly

definitions.text: Behave in a more hysterical way
definitions.meaning: split as two words, it means to act more frantically or crazily
to baffle or perplex someone completely

explanation.surface: Someone's increasingly frantic behaviour leaves everyone baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means act more crazily; as one word it means perplex completely.

clue.text: For every oxygen compound there's a bleach

parts.note: per means for each or for every, as in 'per person'
an oxide is a chemical compound containing oxygen

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: every compound containing oxygen can act as a whitener.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrogen peroxide is widely used to lighten hair and whiten fabrics, so it is a bleaching agent.

clue.text: Television sets left inside? Don't report the truth!

indicators.note: inside says one piece goes within the other

parts.note: tellies is British slang for television sets

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the TV sets were left indoors, then urges a cover-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak falsehoods is the opposite of reporting truthfully.

clue.text: Look cross — front of gate not as high

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: lower means less high

explanation.surface: Someone scowls because the front of the gate sits lower than expected.
explanation.definitionFit: To glower is to stare angrily, which is looking cross.

clue.text: Apprentice on right cricket ground gets commendation

parts.note: THE OVAL is a famous cricket ground in south London

explanation.surface: A trainee working at a cricket ground earns praise from the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Approval is favourable judgement, the same as praise or commendation.

clue.text: Mechanical response about wire

parts.note: RE means about or concerning, as in business letters
flex is British for an insulated electric cable or wire

explanation.surface: An engineer's instinctive reaction concerning some electric cabling.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflex is an automatic, involuntary reaction of the body, done without thought.

clue.text: Make efficient new master file

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version of the word master, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a file is a line of people one behind another

explanation.surface: Instructions to tidy up a computer system by creating a fresh master file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'master file' looks like computing jargon, but 'new' shuffles MASTER into STREAM and 'file' is LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To streamline a process is to simplify it so it runs more efficiently.

clue.text: One way to nourish child (fee blotted out)

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A parent's note about feeding a baby, with a fee crossed out in the margin.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeding a baby milk from a bottle instead of the breast is one method of nourishment.

clue.text: Waste food? The swine will!

parts.note: swine is a plural word for pigs
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks who will eat the leftovers, and the answer is the pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigswill is kitchen scraps and leftovers fed to pigs, so it is food waste.

clue.text: Seeks a time to attract first of shoppers

parts.note: to tempt is to lure or attract

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A shop is looking for the right moment to lure customers in.
explanation.definitionFit: Attempts are tries, and to try for something is to seek it.

clue.text: Big spender in favour of Albert going round mine

indicators.note: going round means the outer letters surround another piece

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
Al is a short form of the name Albert
a dig is an excavation, like a mine

explanation.surface: A lavish spender backs a man called Albert as he tours a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A prodigal person spends money wastefully, like the son in the parable.

clue.text: Engrossed in variety of trees in front of Edward

indicators.note: in front of means the previous pieces come before the next one
a variety of something is a different form of it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Ted is a pet form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward becomes absorbed in studying a range of trees in front of him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' shuffles TREES into TERES; IN comes first and TED, a familiar form of Edward, comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Being absorbed in something means being deeply interested in it.

clue.text: Draughtsman goes up for the prize

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a drawer is one who draws, a draughtsman

explanation.surface: A draughtsman climbs the podium to collect an award.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is something given for achievement, like a prize.

clue.text: Tried putting roast initially in cooker

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a stove is a cooker

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone attempted to put a roast in the oven.
explanation.definitionFit: Strove is the past tense of strive, meaning made an effort or tried.

clue.text: Consort with two men, both short

parts.note: Al and Bert are both shortened forms of men's names
Al and Bert are both shortened forms of men's names

explanation.surface: Someone keeps company with a pair of short men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consort' is the definition: Prince ALBERT was the consort of Queen Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Albert was husband and royal consort to Queen Victoria.

clue.text: Stayed out with regular boyfriend

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stayed out late with their partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A steady is someone you date regularly, a fixed partner.

clue.text: Late back, catching married men making cheese

indicators.note: catching means the outer piece takes the other inside it
back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Late home, someone catches married men making cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the first word round to ETAL; 'catching' then wraps it around the married men, so 'Late' is fodder, not a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmental is a hard Swiss cheese with large holes.

clue.text: Criticise little devil with wrong gun

parts.note: an imp is a small devil

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone finds fault with an impish child for using the wrong gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn is to dispute or attack someone's honesty or claims, a form of criticism.

clue.text: Nip round before archaic sleeveless dress appears

indicators.note: turning round means the word is read backwards

parts.note: afore is an old-fashioned word meaning before

explanation.surface: Someone pops out before an old-fashioned dress turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is a collarless sleeveless dress worn over a blouse or jumper.

clue.text: In the end, stall off youth leader

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are put out of their usual order
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Eventually a market stall is shut down by a young ringleader.
explanation.definitionFit: Lastly means finally, at the close of a list or sequence.

clue.text: Exhausted and late on round

parts.note: late can mean dead, as in 'the late king'
a beat is a regular round, like a police officer's patrol

explanation.surface: Someone is tired out from being late on their rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dead beat is an informal way of saying completely worn out.
